zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical cross-check: supplied NINJAL Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, version 202510, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida (CC BY 4.0). The scan, not the lexical index, determines the transcription. Source: https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; license: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

lines.note: Tsubi is glossed in Latin as the female genitals. The upright final B is the low-register label, not part of the italic anatomical gloss.
Tsubo denotes a jar or pot. Daiku no tsubo begins the carpenter's compound continued below; the printed hyphen belongs to this physical division.
Bo completes daiku no tsubo; sumitsubo is offered as an alternative. The gloss identifies the carpenter's ink container, retaining abbreviated carpĩteiros rather than expanding it.
Here tsubo is the female socket of a hinge. Engonço corrects OCR Engorço; hijitsubo introduces the paired hinge components explained on the following row.
The male and female parts complete the explanation of hijitsubo. This short, indented continuation is not a separate headword.

runs.text: Pateo, ou Niua pequena. Mais or-

lines.note: Tsubo is a courtyard or small niwa. Niua is embedded in Portuguese, and its locally italic appearance is retained. Or- begins ordinariamente across the row break.
Completes the statement that tsubo no uchi is the more usual expression. The second vowel in Tçubono is o, not OCR u; the close Portuguese spacing is retained.

runs.text: Couſa hum pouco apanhada como va

lines.note: Tsuboi describes something drawn inward or constricted, such as a vessel. Va continues as vaso below; no hyphen is supplied merely because the word continues.

runs.text: ſo, & que tem a boca mais eſtreita, & fecha-

lines.note: Completes vaso and specifies a narrower, more closed mouth. The scan supports eſtreita with a single s, not OCR eßtreita; fecha- continues below.
Da completes fechada. Tsubozara is a basin with a constricted opening, and its gloss divides boca across the next row break.
Completes the narrow-mouth description. Tçu- begins tsubosode, whose remaining letters occupy the following physical row.

runs.text: Mangas fechadas que tem a boca

lines.note: Boſode completes tsubosode, sleeves with a narrow opening. The initial b, also supported by the later complete headword, corrects OCR hoſode.
The sleeve opening is small and narrow. The visibly loose internal spacing in pe quena is retained rather than silently regularized.
Tsubome describes closing or narrowing an opening. The scan supports the headword without OCR's extra i and reads Fechar, not Techar; co- belongs to como below.

runs.text: mo beiços, ou abertura dalgũa couſa.

lines.note: Completes como and gives lips or an object's opening as examples of what is narrowed. The tilde in dalgũa is retained over its printed vowel.

runs.text: Eſtar a flor em botão. Vt,

lines.note: The principal forms describe a flower remaining in bud. The Portuguese reads flor, not OCR fler; Vt is italic apparatus introducing the example below.
Hana ga tsubomu illustrates a flower being in bud; the verb has no extra final a. A second sense then begins: people gathering or drawing together.

runs.text: aiuntarſe a gente q̃ eſtaua deſunida, ou eſpa-

lines.note: People who were separated or scattered now assemble. The printed q̃ is not expanded; eſpa- completes espalhada on the next row.
Completes espalhada and supplies ninju ga tsubomu, a group gathering together. Ninjuga is retained without importing a long-vowel mark from a normalized reading.
Tsubomushi is glossed as oução, a small parasitic mite. The example begins tsubomushi ga, with g rather than OCR q and a printed terminal hyphen.

runs.text: Comer, o oução, ou eſtar comendo na

lines.note: Cǔ completes tsubomushi ga kuu, the mite eating or biting. The visible c and caroned u replace the garbled provisional fragment; the Portuguese continues with the affected hand below.
Mão completes the first gloss. The next example describes the mite crawling or progressing; Tçubomuxiga corrects OCR Tçuboiniuxiga, followed by fǒ with a caron.
The oução is the subject of the preceding ir laurando, describing its continuing activity. The noun retains the same cedilla as in the headword gloss.

runs.text: Molher principal que gouerna o in-

lines.note: Tsubone here denotes a senior woman managing a lord's household interior. Principal and que are separate printed words; in- continues interior below.

runs.text: terior da caſa de algum ſenhor.

lines.note: Completes interior: the woman has charge of the inner part of a lord's household. This personal sense is distinct from the room sense below.
This second tsubone is a partitioned room or separate lodging. The worn final e is recoverable from its shape and the adjacent entry; no clear terminal punctuation is supplied after ſepa.

runs.text: rada onde habita algũa molher. ¶ Tambem

lines.note: Rada completes separada: the lodging houses a woman. The next sentence begins Tambem, with T rather than OCR P, and adds another room-related gloss.

runs.text: ſe toma por camara, ou cubiculo de molheres.

lines.note: Tsubone can also mean a women's chamber or small room. Camara is one printed word, not OCR ca mara; this line finishes the second entry.
Tsubonomi names a particular chisel or gouge, described as somewhat bent. Dobra- continues below; the gloss does not establish an exact modern tool classification.

runs.text: do, ou redondo. & apanhado, ou fechado

lines.note: Completes dobrado and adds rounded, drawn-in or closed as descriptions of the tool. The printed punctuation after redondo and absence of a secure final stop are retained.

runs.text: Mangas redondas que tem a boca

lines.note: Tsubosode is independently entered as rounded sleeves with a restricted opening. The definition develops the sleeve example previously given under tsuboi.
The opening is small and gathered inward. This completes the clothing sense, separate from the armour sense in the following entry.
This second tsubosode denotes armour plates rather than ordinary sleeves. The repeated headword corrects OCR Touboſode; the gloss introduces rounded protective plates.

runs.text: que poem como rodelas ſobre os braços dos om-

lines.note: The plates are placed like small shields over the arms, from the shoulders downward. Braços has a cedilla rather than OCR g; om- is completed on the next genuine row.
Completes ombros pera baixo, from the shoulders downward. Provisional c1-l035 duplicated this same physical row; deleting that detection loses no text because the complete reading remains here.
Tsubozumire is identified only as an herb. The brief gloss does not itself establish a botanical species, so none is added.

runs.text: Grão de trigo, arroz, &c, ou cõ-

lines.note: Tsubu is a grain of wheat, rice or similar material. The alternative gloss begins abbreviated cõ-, completed below as contas, beads; the headword's cedilla is visible.
Completes the alternative sense of grain-like beads. Provisional c1-l039 was a garbled duplicate detection of this physical row; the full text remains here.
A separate tsubu is a hill or rise used as a military position. Cõmummente introduces the usual practice explained on the next row.
The army establishes a strong position there. This completes the hill sense, not the earlier grain or bead sense.
Tsubumeki and its principal forms mean muttering between one's teeth. The ending eita is retained as printed rather than modernized.
The alternative is speaking to oneself in irritation. Conſigo corrects OCR conjigõ; the scan does not warrant a final nasal mark.
Tsubure describes being crushed or squashed. Both Portuguese verbs are reflexive, and the abbreviated principal parts retain their printed spacing.
A ripe fig illustrates literal crushing. The figurative example starts kimo ga, with its predicate on the following row.
Kimo ga tsubureta is explained by odoroita, being startled. The explanatory marker is i, not OCR j; Me begins the next example concerning sight.
Me or mimi ga tsubururu is glossed as becoming blind or deaf. Mimiga corrects OCR Miniga, and Cegar corrects Cegas; enſurde- continues below.
Cer completes ensurdecer. Hito no shindai ga tsubururu describes someone's estate or standing being ruined; Fitono corrects OCR Ficono.
Completes destruirse: someone's estate or condition is ruined. This is the last genuine body row in the left column, above the bottom rule.
Tsuburi is equated with atama, the head. The example repeats the headword across the physical break before riga itai.
Completes tsuburi ga itai, having a headache. The Portuguese supplies the same meaning, and this is indented continuation text.
Tsubusa or tsubusana describes something complete and fully set out. Diffu- corrects OCR ciffu- and contrasts a full account with an abridgment.
Completes diffusa and specifies that the material is not abridged. The sentence defines completeness, not merely diffuseness in a negative sense.
Tsubusani is the adverb, explained as minutely or in detail. Miudamente corrects Maidamente; Tçu- begins its example below.
Tsubusani kiita means having heard the whole matter in detail. Ouui and inteira are separate Portuguese words, correcting the provisional fusion.
Tsubute is a thrown stone or stone-throwing blow. Tsubute wo utsu introduces throwing stones, translated below.
The first example means throwing stones. Tsubute ni utsu introduces another object used as the projectile; its Portuguese translation begins A- here.

runs.text: tirar com outra couſa em lugar de pedra, & a

lines.note: Completes atirar: another object is thrown instead of a stone. The final words lead into a grammatical instruction about expressing that object.
The projectile is put in the accusative. Pão belongs with the upright Japanese example naming bread and mochi, not partly inside italic apparatus. Accuſatiuo corrects acauſatiuo.
Completes tsubute ni utsu: throwing bread or mochi. Mochi is embedded in the Portuguese translation and qualifies for whole-word font review; the Japanese example is not marked word by word.
The figurative example treats money as something thrown away. Per met. corrects Per mel.; v- begins the divided verb vtçu.
Completes utsu, with the meaning of spending recklessly and without purpose. The gloss explains the figurative money-throwing image.
Mukai tsubute wo suru describes throwing stones at one another. Pedradas corrects OCR pedralus; the reciprocal phrase continues below.
Completes the reciprocal stone-throwing gloss, one against another. The initial h and full outros correct provisional cũs and outos.

runs.text: Rodela do joelho. Posto que a-

lines.note: Tsububushi is the kneecap. Posto que introduces the ordinary people's alternative pronunciation on the next row; the terminal printed mark is retained.
Completes the concession: ordinary people say tsubushi. The shorter form is then entered separately on the next row.
This noun tsubushi has the same kneecap meaning. Upright X is the regional label, separate from italic Idem and from the unrelated verb below.
Tsubushi, tsubusu and the historical past in -uita mean crushing. Eſborra- continues as esborrachar and corrects OCR eſtorra-.
Completes esborrachar and gives figurative kimo wo tsubusu, being astounded. The loose printed spacing after Q is retained, not interpreted as another Japanese word.
Completes espantarse. Haremono wo tsubusu means bursting a swelling; Fu- begins the Portuguese furar below.

runs.text: rar, ou fazer arrebentar o inchaço.

lines.note: Completes furar: pierce or cause a swelling to burst. Rar corrects OCR tar, and the scanned article belongs with masculine inchaço.
Tsubuyaki and its principal forms mean muttering between one's teeth. The abbreviated dẽ- begins dentes, not the OCR fragment dẽa.

runs.text: tes, ou falar cõſigo agaſtado, ou murmurãdo.

lines.note: Completes dentes and describes irritated speech to oneself or murmuring. Continuous cõſigo and murmurãdo correct misplaced OCR spaces and the erroneous final c.

runs.text: Voz de quem fala aßi por

lines.note: Tsubuyakigoe is the voice of someone muttering thus. The initial is T, not F; aßi has no extra t, and por remains complete at the edge.
Completes the description of irritated speech between the teeth. Agaſtado corrects the OCR's duplicated s without modernizing antre.
Tsuka is raised earth, such as a burial mound. Tçuca and Terra aleuantada correct provisional Fiçuca, Teira and aleuuntada.
Tumulo completes the mound definition with the alternative of a tomb. This short indented row is body text, not furniture.
Tsuka or tsukabashira is a small supporting post. Final ou leads to the alternative word for a prop below.

runs.text: eſpeque que ſe poem pera ſuſtentar de baixo o

lines.note: The post is placed underneath to support a floor. De baixo o corrects the merged OCR baimao; the object continues below.
Completes the floor-support definition. Tsuka wo koo means putting these props in place; the caron is retained, and Por eſtes corrects Poreſhir.
Completes the example: place the supporting struts beneath timber. The plural pontaletes corrects OCR pontaletee.

runs.text: Punhos da eſpada, ou cabo de faca, &c.

lines.note: This tsuka is a sword hilt or knife handle. The final abbreviation includes c, restoring OCR's incomplete &.; this sense differs from mound and support-post.

runs.text: Caſa feita de baixo da terra.

lines.note: Tsuka ana denotes an underground room or dwelling in this gloss. The Portuguese is feita, made, not frita; the Japanese spacing is retained.
Tsukagashira is the pommel of a katana's hilt. Maçaã retains the source's vowel and tilde sequence; Catana is embedded in Portuguese.

runs.text: Parte dos punhos da Catana que

lines.note: Tsukaguchi is the portion of the katana's hilt specified below. Catana is embedded in the explanation, not an independent Japanese example.
Specifies the part beside the sword guard. The aligned st rendering is retained under the project's deferred ligature audit rather than silently normalized.
Tsukai denotes a message or messenger. This is a flush-left headword, not a continuation; Tçu- begins its example below.
Tsukai wo suru means serving as messenger or going on an errand. Another example begins with the divided Tçu- at the edge.
Completes tsukai ni yaru, sending someone with a message. Cõ and recado have a visible boundary, correcting the OCR fusion.
Tsukai, tsukoo and tsukoota are principal forms of using or employing. The first abbreviated form is ǒ without OCR's extra i; this is a new flush-left entry.
Completes the definition and gives hito wo tsukoo, employing someone. The weak mark in tçucô is retained as a circumflex rather than automatically harmonized with adjacent caroned forms.
Completes alguem. Te wo tsukoo introduces a technique, specified below as a fencing movement or lesson; algum ends in m, not OCR n.

runs.text: tempo, ou lição de eſgrima. ¶ Item, Ga-

lines.note: The technique is a fencing movement or lesson. A spending sense then begins with Gastar divided at the physical edge.

Completes Gastar and illustrates spending one's wealth. Zaifôuo has a circumflex, while tçucǒ has a caron. The narrow final nasal in fazem remains less distinct; m is retained from the aligned reading rather than normalized to expected fazen before da below.
Completes the estate or wealth gloss. Nen wo tsukoo means exercising care or attention, and cuida- begins cuidado below.
Completes cuidado and adds applying diligence. This is the last body row; separate lower-right Tçucai- is a catchword, not another headword here.
